initial_failures.reason: A command variable was mutable only in the Windows branch; Linux unused_mut lint failed. Corrected with cfg-scoped shadowing before final gates.

limitations: The actual Windows public-control native gate was prepared but not executed. No retry/bypass of the existing Windows native automatic approval quota rejection. No claim of actual Windows SDK, pipe, host or hardware acceptance.

Most verifier orchestration uses portable std APIs and is compiled/linted on Linux. Two explicit example tests cover descriptor parsing and bounded diagnostics. The actual non-Windows entry returned expected exit78 before path lookup or child launch. This is not a Windows execution substitute.

The modified cfg(windows) fixture body, Windows creation_flags branch and PowerShell -PublicControl runner were not type-checked/executed natively here. Existing Windows active/standby/terminal/console fixture cases must also be re-run for the new snapshot.

Native success requires actual selected host/CLI, kernel pipe/token path, owned no-input worker exit, zero progress and final actual Exited snapshot. A late/missing final snapshot or timeout fails instead of assuming exit/cleanup. Passed marker is created only after all required observations; all case directories/logs are retained.

Fixed executable basenames prevent accidental capture-worker selection but are not image authentication. Trusted source snapshot/manifest and Windows-local validation directory remain premises; same-user deliberate replacement/handle transfer is not proven safe by a filename check.

Verifier only operates on retained Child handles and has bounded memory/output/waits; failure Drop requests kill of its own child without inferring successful exit. No input devices, Hook, driver or injection are used by the designated fixture.

Eight existing Unix IPC tests remain ignored in the default run and were not re-run for this Windows-tooling-only slice. Full migration, GUI Start/Resume/Apply/discovery, native/hardware acceptance, Wayland and packaging remain unfinished.
